Comments specific to an item on the agenda may be heard when that item is considered. Members of the public may address the Commission for up to three minutes. General Public Comment may be continued to the end of the agenda if speakers exceed 15 minutes of General Public Comment.

Consent Calendar of Routine Matters All items listed on the consent calendar are considered routine by the Commission and may be acted upon together by a single vote of the Commission. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a member of the Commission, the public or staff requests its individual consideration. In that case, the item will be removed from the consent calendar and considered individually at this or a future hearing.

items.title: Animal Care and Control Tenant Improvement – Contract Award
items.text: Animal Care and Control Tenant Improvement – Contract Award Staff Recommendation: Award construction contract in the amount of $2,363,330 for 305 consecutive calendar days to Buhler Commercial to perform tenant improvements at the SF Animal Care & Control facility. On March 5, 2024, the Planning Department determined that the activities encompassed under the contract are exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”) as a Class 1 categorical exemption (CEQA Guidelines Section 15301), as described in the determination contained in the Commission’s files for this contract.

items.title: Beale Street Improvement Phase 1 – Contract Award
items.text: Beale Street Improvement Phase 1 – Contract Award Staff Recommendation: Award Beale Street Improvement Project Phase 1 to Esquivel Grading & Paving, Inc., in the amount of $1,841,494 with $184,149 for contingency and a contract duration of 315 consecutive calendar days with 30 consecutive calendar days of contingency; and adopt findings pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act pertaining to the Final Environmental Impact Report for this project, which the Planning Commission certified on May 24, 2012, and adopt the associated Mitigation and Monitoring and Reporting Program. The project consists of a protected, two-way cycle track with raised crosswalks, curb ramps, widening sidewalks, sewer replacement, water and drainage work, streetscape improvements, street lighting, traffic control, and all other related work on Beale Street between Market and Folsom Streets. The award of this contract constitutes the Approval Action for the project as defined in Chapter 31 of the San Francisco Administrative Code.
